page: Google Cloud Platform f1-micro is an entry-level virtual machine belonging to the f1 server family. It features 1 vCPU mapped to a shared physical Intel Xeon core on the x86_64 architecture, with 1 physical core and 1 thread. The instance is equipped with 0.6 GB of system memory, providing 0.6 GB of RAM per core. It does not include any dedicated GPU hardware or local NVMe storage, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 38 MB of L3 cache.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the bottom 10% across all tested categories. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests both scored 384.79. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 80.8 GB/sec, while the large block write speed drops to 0.2 GB/sec. Passmark CPU testing yielded a score of 236.08, with an encryption test score of 73.1 and a physics test score of 33.01. Database operations and general memory scores on Passmark registered at 0.0. For application workloads, the instance achieved 0.24 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks and a static web serving throughput of 0.22 GB/sec.

The f1-micro is designed for high resource density and low-cost utility rather than raw computational power. The primary tradeoff is its shared CPU allocation and extremely constrained 0.6 GB memory capacity, which limits its ability to handle concurrent processes or memory-intensive applications. Given these hardware constraints and low benchmark scores, this server type is best utilized for lightweight background tasks, basic automation scripts, low-traffic static web serving, or simple development and testing environments that do not require sustained CPU performance.
